concerns: Affinity depletion may strip EV-bound proteins or perturb membranes, producing apparent loss or altered capture profiles that mimic improvement (need orthogonal protection assays and intact-EV spike-ins).
Depletion buffers or resin leachables may interfere with immuno-capture assays or particle counting—capture-compatibility controls are essential before interpreting results (MISEV recommendation).

Qualitative yield assessment is vulnerable to subjective interpretation; include quantitative particle- and mass-recovery metrics and predefined acceptance language to avoid false positives/negatives across lots.

Observed sharpening of analytical co-localization may reflect selective retention/removal of specific EV subpopulations rather than true enrichment of intact EVs; compare marker panels (multiple surface markers) and use spike-ins to detect selective loss.

Improved analytical signatures do not guarantee improved in vivo recoverability or delivery — non-human primate data indicate intranasal delivery and cross-species detectability are limited and may dominate downstream translational outcomes.

Ensure paired processing uses identical conditioned-medium lots (>=3 biological lots) and that positive control characterized EVs are processed in parallel to validate assay sensitivity and protection readouts.
conclusion: The proposed head-to-head experiment is a plausible and appropriately targeted test of the fractionation hypothesis: the causal logic (remove high-abundance soluble proteins -> reduce non-vesicular co-elution -> sharpen co-localization of particle peaks with capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive signal) is coherent and the selected orthogonal readouts (fractionated particle counts, intact-capture signal, detergent/protease protection, particle:protein ratio, recovery) are directly linked to the hypothesis. If executed with the specified controls (capture-compatibility checks, detergent/protease protection, negative/positive controls and exogenous intact-EV spike-ins) the experiment should discriminate the main competing explanations (true preservation/enrichment of intact EVs vs. artefactual assay interference or selective loss of EV subpopulations). However, substantial uncertainty remains about (A) whether affinity depletion can be implemented without removing or damaging EVs, (B) whether buffer/resin leachables will confound capture assays, and (C) whether any analytical improvement will translate into in vivo detectability or manufacturable benefit given known species/formulation delivery barriers. Therefore proceed, but require the capture-compatibility and spike-in controls, quantitative recovery metrics, and replication across independent conditioned-medium lots prior to concluding that the pre-SEC depletion path is advantageous.
evidence_gap: No prior direct evidence that a gentle affinity-depletion step implemented pre-SEC preserves intact EV membranes and improves yield while avoiding removal of EV-associated proteins; translational biodistribution and cross-species delivery constraints are unresolved (i.e., analytical improvements may not predict in vivo performance).
